newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs, Germans to apologise in WW2 declaration.
newsitem.headline: Czechs, Germans to apologise in WW2 declaration.

text.p: Germany and the Czech Republic will apologise to each other for Nazi war crimes and for Czech excesses against ethnic Germans after World War Two in a joint declaration, according to a draft of the document obtained by Reuters on Monday.

In the long-awaited declaration, Bonn also strongly backs Czech ambitions to join the European Union (EU) and NATO defence alliance. Diplomats said few changes would be made to the draft which is expected to be initialled by the Czech and German foreign ministers shortly before Christmas.

In the declaration, Bonn apologises for Nazi brutality during the occupation of the former Czechoslovakia while Prague admits that innocent people suffered injustice when the country's 2.5 million Sudeten German minority was expelled en masse after World War Two.

Czech and German negotiators have laboured for about two years to complete the declaration, which aims to close the book on 50 years of mistrust following the war. Many of the delays have been due to objections to the text from Sudeten German groups mostly based in the German state of Bavaria.
Bonn admits that the Nazi occuaption, which began with Hitler's annexation of areas where the Sudetens were in a majority, laid the foundation for the mass expulsions.

"The German side ... is aware of the fact that the National Socialist policy of violence against the Czech people helped to create the basis for the post-war escape, expulsion and forced resettlement," the draft says.
